title: Granular tenant throttle policies and economics brainstorm
content:
Purpose:
- Rapid brain dump for a product + ops playbook that treats tenant throttling as both an availability control and an economic signaling mechanism.
- Goal: produce a small set of experimentable knobs we can ship to Trusted Tenant pilots to reduce noisy neighbors and expose predictable unit economics.

Background / why now:
- Dedicated pools see 2 classes of problematic load: sustained heavy usage (predictable, contractable) and microbursts (short, high QPS spikes). Current coarse tenant quotas + eviction are blunt: they protect SLOs but cause bad UX and churn.
- We need finer controls that: a) preserve latency SLOs, b) let tenants pay for transient capacity, c) reduce manual ops during peak events.

High-level proposal (summary):
1) Localized shaping: per-tenant multi-bucket token leaky buckets (steady, burst, emergency) with different refill rates and costs.
2) Market signals: optional surge price multiplier that applies to burst tokens; surfaced to tenants and used for billing/alerts.
3) Soft fallback lanes: automatic graceful degradation to cheaper model variants or smaller sequence-length fallbacks when burst budget exhausted.
4) Ops-first guardrails: observable health gates, auto-quarantine if a tenant breaches abuse patterns, with manual override.

Design ideas (details):
- Token buckets: each tenant gets: steady_rate (tokens/sec), burst_bucket (size & refill policy), emergency_quota (short TTL emergency tokens).
  - Example: steady_rate=10k tokens/s, burst_bucket=200k tokens, emergency_quota=20k tokens (30s TTL).
  - Burst tokens consumed at X tokens/request, triggers accounting meter.
- Pricing/crediting model: burst tokens can be covered 3 ways: pre-bought credits (discounted), on-demand surge-price (higher rate), or auto-borrow with payback and penalty (for enterprise only).
- Dynamic refill: refill rates can scale with committed capacity and recent usage patterns. E.g., tenants with higher reserved qps get larger steady_rate and slower depletion of burst_bucket.
- Soft fallback actions (order): 1) degrade response length, 2) switch model variant (quantized/cheaper), 3) route to shared capacity (if tier allows), 4) return 429 or low-cost summary.

Operational controls / runbook snippets:
- Detect: continuous token consumption metrics per tenant + heatmap. Threshold rule: if burst_token_consumption > 80% of burst_bucket in 15s -> mark as transient hard-burst event.
- Respond: for hard-burst event: apply temporary shaping (50% steady_rate), ring Ops alert, start surge-billing meter.
- Escalate: if unusual pattern repeats >3 times in 24h, auto-schedule tenant to "surge review" (sales + SE).
- Quarantine: if tenant exhibits ratios typical of misuse (e.g., high retry rates, constant small payloads with enormous token counts), isolate to a hardened lane and require remediation.

Metrics to track (minimum):
- per-tenant steady_token_rate, burst_bucket_level, burst_consumption_rate
- per-tenant burst_cost (currency), if surge-pricing enabled
- tail latency 50/95/99 for tenants under shaping vs baseline
- number of automatic fallbacks and user-visible error rates (4xx/5xx)
- ops interventions per tenant per month

Experiment matrix (quick wins):
A) Billing signal pilot: enable surge price only (no auto-shaping). Observe conversion: % tenants who purchase auto-burst credits.
B) Soft-shape pilot: enable shaping + fallback but no billing. Measure latency uptime improvements and customer complaints.
C) Full pilot: shaping + surge billing + soft fallback + manual ops alerts. Compare cost-to-serve delta.

Mock tenant config examples (for dev/test):
- small-saas: steady=2k t/s, burst_bucket=50k, emergency=5k, surge_allowed=true, fallback_to=model-x-small
- mid-market: steady=20k, burst_bucket=500k, emergency=50k, surge_allowed=true, fallback_to=model-x-medium
- enterprise: steady=200k, burst_bucket=5M, emergency=200k, surge_enabled=auto-borrow, fallback_to=model-x-large

Edge cases & constraints:
- Billing latency: surge-price applied in near-real-time but invoice reconciliation may lag; need clear tenant-facing UI showing accrued surge usage.
- Cross-tenant fairness: avoid policies that let wealthy tenants permanently starve others; limit concurrent burst budgets across a pool via pool-wide headroom guard.
- Predictive accuracy: predictive warmup making refill decisions requires conservative thresholds to avoid oscillation.

Open questions / trade-offs (we should debate):
- Transparency vs control: how much should tenants see vs what we hide? Full transparency could help customers self-manage but may increase support overhead.
- Penalties: is a monetary penalty for repeated abuse better than throttling? How does that interact with enterprise SLAs and contracts?
- Complexity: can we keep UI simple? Too many knobs will confuse customers and ops. Aim for 3 default profiles + advanced custom config.
- Interop with Dedicated autoscaler: how do allocator and shaping interact? Should autoscaler treat burst tokens as pressure signals to scale pre-warm?

Next immediate steps (owner: Aisha):
- Draft a short experiment PRD (1 pager) for the Billing signal pilot (due 2w).
- Get toy implementation from infra: token meter + simple surge_price flag in serving-runtime (spike: Marco).
- UX: Leah to mock a tenant dashboard widget for burst balances + projected surge cost.
- Stakeholders: loop in sales + legal for enterprise auto-borrow guardrails.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Prototype early with a single dedicated pool serving 3 pilot tenants.
- Build Grafana dashboards keyed by tenant + pool.
- Create synthetic load tests to validate fallback latencies and billing correctness.

References / similar docs:
- see infra PR about meters: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1420
- linear ticket INF-593 for pricing experiment plan

Rough UX copy to add to tenant console (draft):
- "Burst balance: 120k tokens remaining (refills daily). Surges incur 2.5x rate unless covered by credits."
- "Auto-borrow: allow temporary overdrafts for mission-critical traffic. Overdrafts are repayable and may incur penalties per your contract."

Long-term vision (1yr):
- Tenants can trade/buy burst credits via API; markets for seasonal workloads; ability to stake reserved capacity across accounts.
- A small marketplace for temporary capacity: trusted partners can rent pool headroom during low-util windows.

Unresolved: which internal SLA tiers map to which default refill/credit policies (ask product ops + finance).

---
Patchy draft, will refine after we see infra feasibility. Comments inline welcome.
